headline: EU approves Italian bank UniCredit’s takeover of Germany’s Commerzbank
summary: The European Commission approved on Monday 16 November, without conditions, UniCredit’s plan to take control of Commerzbank. It found the deal raises no competition problems in the EU.
why: It would be one of the biggest cross-border bank deals in Europe and create a stronger European lender, a goal the EU supports. The takeover has faced resistance in Germany, where Commerzbank is one of the largest banks.

event.t: The European Commission cleared the deal under EU merger rules on Monday 16 November, without asking for any changes.
The European Central Bank had already approved the takeover in October.
EU competition chief Teresa Ribera said “Europe needs stronger banks” that can compete and grow.
UniCredit has pursued Commerzbank for more than two years, building up its stake despite opposition in Germany.

effects.label: UniCredit
effects.t: A key approval for its takeover plan.

effects.t: A step toward bigger banks that work across EU borders.
